folkways.perk.building_fortune.desc: Blocks broken with a tool drop as if it had Fortune I/II/III; a tool with higher Fortune keeps its own. Prospecting finds are unaffected.
folkways.perk.building_prospecting.desc: Mining ordinary stone has an 4/7/11%% chance to find a mineral weighted by the local biome, height and ore generation settings. Rank III has a 15%% chance of a second find.
folkways.perk.building_quarrying.desc: Consecutive mining of the same ordinary stone builds up to +15/30/50%% excavation speed after 8 blocks. A 10-second pause resets momentum.
folkways.perk.building_tool_expert.desc: Building and excavation tool durability consumption -15/30/45%%.
folkways.perk.crafting_batch.desc: Complete 2/3/4 runs of one recipe per operation, consuming all materials.
folkways.perk.crafting_byproducts.desc: Eligible recipes have a 10%%/20%%/30%% chance to yield their configured byproduct.
folkways.perk.crafting_frugal.desc: Eligible recipes refund each ingredient unit with an 5%%/10%%/15%% chance; packing recipes excluded.
folkways.perk.crafting_furnace.desc: Input batches personally loaded smelt 10%%/20%%/30%% faster.
folkways.perk.farming_bountiful.desc: Primary crop yield +10%% / 20%% / 35%%. Separate seed drops are unchanged.
folkways.perk.farming_care.desc: Planted and replanted crops grow 10%% / 20%% / 35%% faster. One treatment per crop.
folkways.perk.farming_chain_harvest.desc: Harvest 1 / 2 / 4 additional adjacent mature crops in the field, respecting reserved jobs.
folkways.perk.farming_replant.desc: Replant during harvest, saving 0%% / 15%% / 30%% of seeds.
folkways.perk.fishing_school.desc: Fish catches have a 15%% / 25%% / 40%% chance of 1 / 1 / 2 extra fish of the same species.
folkways.perk.fishing_treasure.desc: Successful catches have a 2%% / 4%% / 6%% chance of an extra local discovery, controlled by loot tables.
folkways.perk.fishing_water_sense.desc: Progressively favors uncommon fish from the active local fishing loot table.
folkways.perk.herding_breeder.desc: Resident-assisted breeding has a 5%% / 10%% / 20%% chance of twins, within the pasture target.
folkways.perk.herding_butcher.desc: Ordinary carcass products +15%% / 30%% / 50%%. Special drops are unchanged.
folkways.perk.herding_fleece.desc: Shearing yields 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 extra wool of the original color on average.
folkways.perk.herding_nurture.desc: Feeding a juvenile additionally reduces remaining growth time by 10%% / 20%% / 30%%, once per animal.
folkways.perk.patrolling_alert.desc: Detect threats 2/4/6 blocks farther away and share targets with nearby patrollers.
folkways.perk.patrolling_martial.desc: Deal 10%%/20%%/35%% more damage to hostile creatures.
folkways.perk.patrolling_reassuring.desc: Wards grant residents +2/4/6 safety mood and make attack distress fade 20%%/40%%/60%% faster.
folkways.perk.patrolling_stalwart.desc: Take 5%%/10%%/20%% less damage from hostile creatures.

folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.header: Building: draw it, and the colony raises it
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_1: With the book marking out, frame the ground and pick Pattern from what the box can become. A line drawn with the book offers it too.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_2: Then choose a pattern and its few settings, down to the blocks it is made of. Folkways ships a few, data packs add more under folkways/pattern, and your own go in the folkways/pattern folder of your game.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_3: Residents with the building trade take the order. First they clear what stands where the drawing wants empty space, working down from the top. Containers are emptied into the colony's stores before their blocks go.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_4: Then they lay it from the bottom up, a cell at a time, with blocks fetched from the colony's stores.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_5: While you hold the book, the blocks still to go show as ghosts, and a card over the site counts the cells laid and lists, under Still needs, what the rest will take.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_6: A cell with nowhere in reach to stand gets a column of scaffolding beside it, taken from the stores. Once that part is laid it comes down, and the scaffolding goes back.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_7: The Building page lists every build order with its cells done out of the total. Deleting one stops the work and takes any scaffolding it put up back down.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_8: The mine is drawn all at once from the ground as it stands, and filed as one ordinary build order.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.building.text_9: In creative mode, a drawing you confirm stands up at once.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.creative_supplie: Creative supplies: only what the task needs
Place and configure a creative supply box in Creative mode. Choose all items, or a whitelist of items, tags and searches.
Mark the box with the colony book. It supplies tasks; mark an ordinary chest separately to store their finished goods.
Residents walk to the box and take only the finite amount their current job needs. A full pack or an unreachable box waits.
For a full production-chain test, whitelist base ingredients only and order the final dish. Intermediate foods and finished dishes must be made by the residents.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.damage_control.h: Damage control: put out fires and restore missing blocks
folkways_vanilla.ponder.damage_control.t: Hold the Colony Book, press V and choose Damage Control. Mark two corners and protect the area. Allow residents to work in damage control; fleeing danger still comes first.

Workers smother nearby fire without placing water. With Create: FireFighting Additions installed, they prefer a hydrant cabinet with a hose, nozzle and water, or borrow and refill an extinguisher. Spraying uses the addon’s native mist and water effects.
Right-click a protected area to open its zone settings. Use Reset baseline and enable repairs. Hover the colored markers to inspect fires, missing blocks, conflicts and workers.
Containers, crops, fluids and machines stay out of the baseline. Different blocks are reported as conflicts. After remodelling, use Reset baseline in the zone settings.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.header: Dining: set a table for the colony
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.text_1: With the book marking out, frame a dining area around tables and adjacent chairs. Use supported mod tables; bottom stairs make chairs. Include the chairs in the area and leave a clear aisle beside them.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.text_2: Connected table tops on the same level form one table. Residents can serve it from any reachable edge and eat from any free chair beside it; they do not need to reach each dish separately.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.text_3: Choose food and 1 to 4 servings per table cell in the area settings. Tables with an inventory use that many slots, up to their capacity. Supported tables without inventories hold one placed dish, such as cake.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.text_4: Residents bring the chosen food from colony supplies or arrange its production, then set the table. Hungry neighbours take a free place and eat. Keep ingredients and a route to the table available.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.dining.text_5: The drink list is separate from food. With compatible bar furniture installed, dining areas stock supported drink counters automatically. Diners fetch a drink with their meal; ordinary storage cabinets can instead be stocked by delivery orders.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.header: Farming: draw a plot, and let it come back
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_1: With the book marking out, click two opposite corners to frame a plot. Its settings say what it grows, wheat here, and whether residents pull up grass and flowers before hoeing; both are on to start.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_2: Residents hoe the ground inside the box. A hoe is the one tool a plot asks for, and the tool list on the Farming page has to allow it: an empty list allows none.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_3: Then they sow it, and come back when the crop is ripe. Crops that don't need farmland, like cane or saplings, are sown without hoeing.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_4: Most crops leave the soil bare once harvested, and the next round is sown on the same ground.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_5: Sugar cane is cut once it stands three tall, bamboo at four, and only down to the bottom stalk. What stays keeps growing on its own. Bamboo is sown two rows at a time with an aisle left between, so nobody is walled in.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_6: Melons and pumpkins give up the fruit only. The vine is left standing and grows another one. Vines are sown a cell in from the edge of the plot, and the fruit grows in the ring left round them.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_7: A wood lot is a plot whose crop is a sapling. The same cycle: every log of the tree is felled with the leaves it holds up, all of it carried off, and a sapling goes back where one has room to grow. Dark oak goes in four to a square, and jungle and spruce can too.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.farming.text_8: A farmer with the Replant perk resows as they harvest, using a seed from what the crop just dropped. It only works for crops cut down whole, like wheat, not for cane, fruit or trees.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.header: Fishing: frame the bank, not the water
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_1: A fishery frames the bank the residents stand on.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_2: Never the water itself. Frame the bank, and the water within reach of it is what gets fished.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_3: Each fishery fishes the one block of water nearest its bank, and two fisheries never share one. If that block is already taken, the second fishery sits idle.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_4: A rod is the one tool a cast asks for, and it has to be on the tool list on the Fishing page.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_5: Then they stand there and wait out the bite. The line running to the float is how you tell fishing apart from idling.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.fishing.text_6: Practice shortens the wait: the Skilled Angler perk brings the bite on sooner.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.groundwork.heade: Groundwork: mark a box, and the ground in it is worked
folkways_vanilla.ponder.groundwork.text_: Clear or Fill turns the zone into one build order, then erases the zone. With Fill ticked, every marked cell targets the chosen block. Other work ticked is ignored.
Clear alone orders air at every marked cell. The zone disappears as soon as the order is filed; builders then excavate it as an ordinary build site.
Fill orders the chosen block at every marked cell, replacing whatever stands there. The zone disappears when filed; builders bring the blocks from the colony's stores.
With Clear and Fill off, Weed pulls grass and ferns. Flowers are pulled only with Pull flowers ticked. Farmers do it.

Fell takes down trees whose trunks stand in the box, leaves and all. It also clears horizontal logs resting on the ground away from trees, with their moss and other small plants. Colony building blocks stay.
Haul has the haulers pick up whatever lies loose in the box and carry it off to the colony's stores.

Forage has farmers break food plants and store all their drops. Young berry bushes and fruitless cave-vine segments are cleared too. The marked vine column is removed, without leaving plants to regrow. Clear takes priority when both switches are ticked.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_1: Join beds to the colony with the book. Residents automatically claim a free bed; the Human residents page lists those still unclaimed.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_2: Walking tires him, and so does standing at work. Tired enough, he goes back to his own bed and sleeps it off. Without a bed of his own he cannot sleep, and his housing mood is poor.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_3: Work and walking consume food; time spent working and distance walked build fatigue.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_4: The colony keeps food for three days in each resident's pack, and he eats when hungry. On the Human residents page, choose allowed foods or exclusions and whether food safety filters apply.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_5: With no allowed food in colony stores, his pack stays empty. A starving resident loses health.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_6: Hold the book, and the card over each resident nearby shows a drumstick for how full he is and a moon for how rested.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.household.text_7: Hold the book to see a card over each colony bed: who sleeps there, its room grade, and advice for improving it.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.header: Housing: a room worth coming home to
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_1: Enclose the beds under a roof, with a door residents can walk through. Every open floor cell needs light of at least 8. Without these, or with fewer than four floor blocks per bed, it is only a basic bed.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_2: A suitable dormitory has at least four floor blocks per bed. For comfortable housing, allow six per bed, no more than four beds, and at least two furnishing kinds.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_3: An excellent bedroom allows up to two beds, with nine floor blocks per bed and at least three furnishing kinds. Storage, carpet, decoration and tables are the four kinds; extra copies of one kind do not count again.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_4: Keep production blocks out of an excellent bedroom. A crafting table or furnace bars the top grade even when there is enough space and furniture. Hold the book to read each bed's grade and advice.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_5: The glyph after a resident's name shows his mood: sad below 40, neutral from 40 to 69, happy from 70. With the book held, happy or angry sparks show when a reason turns into a bonus or penalty.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.housing.text_6: Mood changes work speed gradually: ×0.75 at mood 0, normal speed at 60, and ×1.15 at 100. Better housing helps, along with food, rest, company and recreation.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.header: Orders: name what you want kept, the colony works out the rest
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_1: An order keeps one item stocked in one container. Use the colony book on one of the colony's chests, and the Orders page that opens files the draft into that chest.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_2: The draft is an item, a Refill below mark and a Fill to count.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_3: Maintain files it as a standing order: once the chest drops below the refill mark, it is filled back up to the Fill to count. Deliver fills it to that count once, and the order is done.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_4: You order the finished goods. Fetching the grain and working it at a crafting table, stonecutter or smithing table of the colony's is the colony's business.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_5: What must be smelted goes through a furnace, blast furnace or smoker of the colony's, kept fed from the fuel list on the Workshop page: coal and charcoal, to start with.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_6: Nobody goes out to dig for an order. If the stores hold neither the goods nor what they are made from, it waits.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_7: To withdraw an order, use the colony book on its chest and press Del beside it on the Orders page.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.orders.text_8: Whitelists, blacklists and Allow storing apply only to ordinary resident storage. Orders bypass them, and you can change these settings at any time.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.header: Pastures: keep breeders and harvest grown surplus
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_1: Frame a pen the way you frame a plot. Choose its animal (cows, sheep, pigs or chickens), how many adults to retain from 0 to 64, and whether to shear.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_2: The Pastures page lists every pen: its animal, total head, retained adult target and current grown head. Young animals are included in the total.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_3: Below or at the target, residents feed ready adults in pairs. At the target, breeding continues for one surplus calf; feeding then waits while the surplus grows.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_4: Only grown head above the retained adult target are culled. With a target of four, six grown cows provide two carcasses; a calf never costs the herd a retained adult. A target of 0 clears every grown animal.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_5: Milk is drawn only when something in the colony asked for milk, and each cow gives it once a day.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_6: While the shear switch is on, sheep are shorn once their wool is back, and the shears must be on the tool list on the Pasture page. In a chicken pen, eggs are picked up where they fall.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.pasture.text_7: A gap in the fence shows on the pasture's card in red. A beast that walks off the ground you framed stops being counted, and the pen breeds back up to the target.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.recreation.text_: In quiet moments residents stroll around nearby. Where flowers grow they stop and relax a while, which restores more leisure than a plain walk.
Chatting with a neighbour and spending time with pets restore leisure too. Residents choose these activities themselves, and may take a short break when leisure runs very low.

Pets may visit once at least three residents have beds in rooms graded suitable dormitory or better. Every half-day brings a chance, with mob spawning enabled and a safe place nearby; a visit is not guaranteed.

The colony can attract one pet per three well-housed residents: cats at three, wolves join the pool at six, parrots at ten. They arrive untamed. Residents also enjoy healthy pets tamed by colony members.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.header: Residents: who comes, what they take on, how they look
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_1: A newcomer needs room: a free bed joined with the book, and stored food for every resident plus one more mouth.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_2: Someone must also be waiting. Newcomers gather over time, more slowly as the colony grows, and only a few wait at once. Let one in on the Human residents page brings the next, unless the server has switched arrivals off.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_3: On the Workforce tab each resident has a cell per trade: click it to allow or forbid that trade, scroll it to rank it 1 to 4. You rank trades, never tasks, and a forbidden trade is never handed to him.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_4: Working a trade earns experience. Each level draws a trade perk; levels 3, 6 and 10 also draw a shared perk, such as a brisker walk or a bigger pack. Open the resident's window to read his trades, levels and perks.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_5: A newcomer's name and look are drawn from this colony's name pool and look pool. Either pool can be edited entry by entry, or replaced whole by a set a data pack offers. After that, a resident's own window changes his name, surname and look one by one.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_6: Struck by a mob or a player, or caught by fire, a resident drops what he is at and runs away from it.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.residents.text_7: If a resident dies, everyone who keeps the colony is told.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.header: The workshop: stations the colony works
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_1: Point the book at a crafting table, a stonecutter or a smithing table and it joins the colony as a station. A furnace, blast furnace or smoker joins the same way.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_2: A station needs a spot within reach and in sight of it for a resident to stand on. One walled in on every side is left out.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_3: Residents with the crafting trade work them. They make what the colony's orders call for, and fetch the ingredients from its stores first.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_4: The stonecutter works its own recipes. The smithing table is used for upgrades only, never for trims.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_5: At a furnace they put in a load and come back for it once it is cooked. A large batch is shared out among the idle furnaces of the same kind.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_6: A loaded furnace that has gone cold gets fuel one piece at a time, and only what is on the fuel list: coal and charcoal to begin with.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_7: Anything left finished in a furnace that nobody is waiting on gets taken out too, so the next load has room.
folkways_vanilla.ponder.workshop.text_8: The Workshop page counts the stations and lists each one, a furnace with the fuel in it or No fuel. The fuel list is the first row there.
mod.folkways_vanilla.name: Folkways
folkways.combat.supply_help: Equipment comes from the assigned profile. Each resident collects their own physical set.
